Comparing selection rules by simulation

Source: vignettes/selection.Rmd
selection.Rmd
library(OncoCohortSelect)

Two single-arm cohorts, Cohort1 and Cohort2, are run in parallel, and one of them is to be selected for further development. Cohort2 is the default, and Cohort1 is selected only if the data favor it. This vignette compares decision rules based on the posterior benefit-risk score and on win statistics by their selection probabilities in simulated trials.

What makes a rule better

The scores of the two approaches are on different scales, so their raw values cannot be compared. A fair comparison fixes, for every rule, the probability of selecting Cohort1 when it is not better than Cohort2 (here, identical cohorts), and then compares the probabilities of selecting Cohort1 when it is better. The truth must be defined before the simulation and independently of the rules: by scenarios in which the better cohort is clear (one cohort at least as good on every endpoint), and, for trade-offs between efficacy and safety, by the choice the clinical team would make for the true parameters.

Scenarios

Each scenario gives the true parameters of the two cohorts: PFS and OS medians, response rate and adverse event rate. The number of simulated trials is kept small so that the vignette builds quickly; an evaluation would use several thousand.

make_arm <- function(pfs, orr, os) {
  CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = pfs, orr = orr, resp.cor = 0.4,
                            death.prop = 0.15, os.median = os)
}
scenarios <- list(
  "Identical" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15),
                                 Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),
  "Cohort1 better" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),
                                      Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),
  "Cohort1 better, more AE" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),
                                               Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)),
                                   ae = c(0.40, 0.20)))
nsim <- 200

Rules

The benefit-risk score against target values is computed for each cohort, and Cohort1 is selected when its score exceeds that of Cohort2 by more than a threshold (br_diff). The score of Cohort1 relative to Cohort2 selects Cohort1 when it exceeds a threshold (br_ref). The net treatment benefit (ntb) and the win ratio (wr) of the pairwise comparisons with priority OS, PFS, response and adverse event select Cohort1 when they exceed a threshold.

eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
  Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                   target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA))
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10))

Each scenario is simulated with 50 patients per cohort, enrolled over 12 months and analyzed at month 24.

res <- lapply(seq_along(scenarios), function(i) {
  sc <- scenarios[[i]]
  d <- SimCohorts(nsim = nsim, n = c(50, 50), arms = sc$arms, ae.rate = sc$ae,
                  cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = i)
  SimSelection(d, eps, crit, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2",
               criteria.ref = crit_ref)
})
names(res) <- names(scenarios)
head(res[["Cohort1 better"]][, c("br_trt", "br_ctl", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr")])
#>      br_trt     br_ctl    br_ref    ntb       wr
#> 1 0.9840167 0.28027139 0.9715141 0.3432 2.083333
#> 2 0.9974228 0.49534396 0.9086497 0.2996 1.884298
#> 3 0.6395187 0.20092152 0.6444149 0.1872 1.470352
#> 4 0.9667704 0.15834083 0.8852263 0.2728 1.761161
#> 5 0.9354467 0.85477364 0.7301443 0.1120 1.262911
#> 6 0.8789330 0.09728543 0.7966242 0.3912 2.323410

Thresholds and selection probabilities

The thresholds are calibrated in the scenario with identical cohorts so that Cohort1 is selected in at most 10% of the trials.

stats <- c("br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr")
thr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stats, function(s) {
  CalibrateThreshold(res[["Identical"]], s, alpha = 0.10)
}))
thr
#>   statistic alpha threshold p_treatment
#> 1   br_diff   0.1 0.4294910         0.1
#> 2    br_ref   0.1 0.5583376         0.1
#> 3       ntb   0.1 0.1492000         0.1
#> 4        wr   0.1 1.3549001         0.1
tab <- sapply(names(res), function(sc) {
  vapply(seq_along(stats), function(i) {
    SelectionOC(res[[sc]], stats[i], threshold = thr$threshold[i])$p_treatment
  }, numeric(1))
})
rownames(tab) <- stats
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 2,
             caption = "Probability of selecting Cohort1 at the calibrated thresholds")
Probability of selecting Cohort1 at the calibrated thresholds
Identical Cohort1 better Cohort1 better, more AE
br_diff 0.1 0.55 0.07
br_ref 0.1 0.84 0.34
ntb 0.1 0.66 0.65
wr 0.1 0.67 0.65

In the scenario “Cohort1 better”, the rules select Cohort1 with probabilities between 0.55 and 0.84. With more adverse events in Cohort1, the probabilities range from 0.07 to 0.65; whether Cohort1 should be selected in that scenario is a clinical judgment that has to be fixed before the rules are compared.

Saturation of the score against target values

In the scenario “Cohort1 better”, the median scores against the target values are 0.936 for Cohort1 and 0.441 for Cohort2. The score measures how certainly a cohort exceeds the targets, not by how much. When both cohorts clearly exceed the targets, both scores approach 1 and their difference carries little information; the score relative to the other cohort and the win statistics compare the cohorts directly.

summary(res[["Cohort1 better"]][, c("br_trt", "br_ctl")])
#>      br_trt           br_ctl       
#>  Min.   :0.3850   Min.   :0.03947  
#>  1st Qu.:0.8613   1st Qu.:0.27401  
#>  Median :0.9358   Median :0.44141  
#>  Mean   :0.9010   Mean   :0.45764  
#>  3rd Qu.:0.9731   3rd Qu.:0.64196  
#>  Max.   :0.9996   Max.   :0.91864
